cards.canonical_statement: Starting at -3 degrees and falling 5 degrees gives -8 degrees.

cards.proof_strategy: Represent the starting temperature and the decrease as signed numbers, then subtract.
sketch_steps: model: Represent three degrees below zero by -3.
change: Subtract 5 for the temperature fall.

cards.canonical_statement: For nonnegative real x, the rectangle with side lengths x and 3 has perimeter 2x+6.
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMBIND><OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="x"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"/><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="leq"/><OMI>0</OMI><OMV name="x"/></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="times"/><OMI>2</OMI><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"/><OMV name="x"/><OMI>3</OMI></OMA></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="times"/><OMI>2</OMI><OMV name="x"/></OMA><OMI>6</OMI></OMA></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: Translate perimeter as twice the sum of adjacent sides and distribute the factor two.

cards.canonical_statement: For real A, l, and nonzero w, if A=lw then l=A/w.
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMBIND><OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="A"/><OMV name="l"/><OMV name="w"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"/><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="and"/><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMV name="A"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="times"/><OMV name="l"/><OMV name="w"/></OMA></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="neq"/><OMV name="w"/><OMI>0</OMI></OMA></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMV name="l"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="divide"/><OMV name="A"/><OMV name="w"/></OMA></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: Treat A=lw as an area formula and divide by the nonzero width to isolate the length.
sketch_steps: premise: Use A=lw and record w≠0.
transform: Divide both sides by w.

cards.canonical_statement: For every nonnegative real x, if x squared is 144 then x is 12.
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMBIND><OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="x"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"/><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="and"/><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="leq"/><OMI>0</OMI><OMV name="x"/></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="power"/><OMV name="x"/><OMI>2</OMI></OMA><OMI>144</OMI></OMA></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMV name="x"/><OMI>12</OMI></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: Use the nonnegative square-root convention and verify that 12 squared is 144.
sketch_steps: solve: The algebraic roots are 12 and -12.

cards.canonical_statement: The nonnegative diagonal d whose square equals 3 squared plus 4 squared has length 5.
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMBIND><OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="d"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"/><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="and"/><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="leq"/><OMI>0</OMI><OMV name="d"/></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="power"/><OMV name="d"/><OMI>2</OMI></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="power"/><OMI>3</OMI><OMI>2</OMI></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="power"/><OMI>4</OMI><OMI>2</OMI></OMA></OMA></OMA></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMV name="d"/><OMI>5</OMI></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: Model a right-triangle diagonal with the Pythagorean relation and take the nonnegative root.
sketch_steps: compute: Simplify the right side to 25.
interpret: The nonnegative solution is d=5.

cards.canonical_statement: For nonnegative real x, the rectangle with sides x+2 and x+3 has area x squared plus 5x plus 6.

cards.proof_strategy: Translate rectangle area as a product of side expressions and expand the product.
sketch_steps: expand: Multiply each term and combine the two linear terms.
